prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, in which magic-wavelength trapping allows many atoms to be interrogated at once and brought optical frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: B049 with Katori and Ye as a single-part prize. Having read all eight round-1 statements and the chair summary, the case still rests on three things. First, the idea is specific and was tested: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice cancels the light shift while many atoms are interrogated in parallel, which is what made the step change in stability and accuracy possible. Second, the demonstration is decisive: Ye's strontium programme took the lattice clock to the 10^-18 regime, and independent laboratories and species, together with direct clock-to-clock comparisons, confirm it. Lindroth and Kroll, who judge the polarizability and blackbody-shift physics from inside the field, both regard the atomic-structure case as sound. Third, the credit divides into concept and demonstration without forcing anyone out of a three-name limit, and the citation can be written around the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice so that it is distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize on controlling single quantum systems. I do not count the three-to-four split in the round-1 files as evidence for either side. The case for B009 is scientifically strong and I hold it as my first alternative, but I judge that its open interpretation makes waiting the better course, whereas B049 loses nothing from being decided now.
statement.case_against: The most serious objection is still distinctness. Frequency combs (2005) and ion control (2012) cover the enabling technology and the lineage, Ye was trained in the comb tradition, and the fundamental-physics output of lattice clocks so far consists of null tests, so some will say this is a decisive improvement in measurement rather than a discovery. The redefinition of the second has not happened, and I cannot say that waiting for it would be wrong, only that it is an administrative event and not part of the discovery. Credit is not uncontested: Lemonde, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups made real contributions, and the record accuracy figures supplied in the candidate material have not been independently checked by anyone on the committee, myself included. Finally, B009 has the broadest opening support, and if the committee concludes that new quantum matter outweighs a refinement of measurement, that is a legitimate scientific judgement that I would not dismiss.

responses.point: Danielsson holds B009 first and says the pairing mechanism is the main reason a committee might wait, while accepting that B049 or B026 are better established; he also notes that the Bistritzer-MacDonald chain gives a natural theory-plus-experiment split.
responses.response: The chair summary asks whether an equal maturity standard is being applied to B009 and B049, and I should answer it directly. I do not ask B009 to have a settled pairing mechanism, since a discovery does not need one. What I do weigh is that the observed phases and the sample dependence are still being sorted out at about eight years, whereas the lattice-clock record rests on a fully accounted error budget compared across laboratories over two decades. That is a difference in how much of the claimed result could still change, not a double standard. I agree with him that the theory-plus-experiment split in B009 is clean, and I would accept a B009 outcome as a sound one. I would, however, ask him to say whether a clearly worded citation, resting on the flat bands and the observed states and not on the mechanism, would remove his own maturity worry.

responses.point: Eriksson holds that the Bistritzer-MacDonald magic-angle condition is the decisive prediction that guided experiment, that a discovery does not need a settled mechanism, and that B026 or B012 would be an acceptable fallback if a stricter maturity bar is set.
responses.response: I accept his point on priority and have revised my round-1 view: the quantitative magic-angle condition is what was tested, so the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto antecedent is less damaging to the theory credit than I implied, and I no longer count it among my main objections. My remaining difference with him is about experimental credit, because Cao, Dean, Young and Yacoby are outside a three-name configuration and the supplied credit does not explain why Jarillo-Herrero stands for all of them. That is a real allocation gap, though a smaller one than for B026. I also note that he names B026 and B012 as fallbacks and not B049, so I would like to know whether he sees a specific weakness in B049 that I have not understood, or whether it is a field outside his expertise.

responses.point: Lindroth holds B049 first, says the polarizability and blackbody-shift physics are checkable from her own field, argues that waiting for the redefinition of the second would reward administrative timing, and admits a bias toward atomic structure.
responses.response: I value her technical judgement on the atomic-structure side and I discount it only slightly for the bias she herself names, since the arguments she gives are checkable by others. I agree that the redefinition is not the discovery and that I should not treat it as a precondition. Where I would press her is the chair summary question about which accuracy and stability results should be verified first. I propose that the committee check the published systematic uncertainty budgets for the strontium lattice clocks at JILA and in Katori's group, the direct comparisons between independent lattice clocks, and the millimetre-scale redshift measurement, and that the citation not quote a record number until that has been done. I would also ask her whether the committee should name 10^-18 as an accuracy or a stability figure, because the two are not interchangeable.

responses.point: Kroll holds B049 first with the same two names, regards the Katori concept and Ye demonstration as a clean split, and discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, near Ye's environment, asking the committee to decide whether it requires recusal on B049.
responses.response: The chair summary asks whether his Hall connection changes how B049 is handled. On what he reports, a past stay in a laboratory linked to the JILA environment with no collaboration with Katori or Ye is a professional proximity that should be on the record, and I would not require recusal from it. I would, however, ask him to state whether he has any continuing tie to JILA, since that would change my view. I also agree with him that Lemonde, Ludlow and the national laboratories have arguable claims and that the committee should decide openly to omit them and not leave the matter implicit. Where we differ slightly is on B012: he keeps it as an alternative, and I do not, because the Zoller, Cirac and Greiner allocation is harder than anything in B049.

responses.point: Johansson has moved from B040 to B012 with Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, arguing that the Jaksch-Zoller proposal, the Mott transition and quantum gas microscopy form a clear chain with two decades of replication, while admitting that Cirac and Jaksch are left out and that the analogue-simulation payoff is undelivered.
responses.response: I agree that B012 is mature and replicated and that the question of what it has discovered is answerable: a quantum phase transition and directly imaged correlations in a tunable many-body system. My objection is that the credit is not yet resolved. He proposes Zoller for the theory, Mehlig proposes Cirac, and Jaksch, who wrote the original proposal with Zoller, is outside the list, so the theory credit changes with whom one asks. The topic is also close to the 2001 condensate prize and the 2012 prize on control of single quantum systems, which is the same distinctness problem I face with B049 but with less clear separation. I would take B012 seriously if he can say which of the three theory names the experiments actually implemented, and I would not treat it as a placeholder for B040 now that he has withdrawn that from his own position.

responses.point: Mehlig holds B009 first, now accepting that the 2018 observation by Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed that a single geometric knob can drive strongly correlated states, and he argues that a discovery does not need a settled mechanism while naming B049 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I give his statistical-physics view of the platform weight, and I agree that a single tuning knob on a clean two-dimensional system is a real conceptual advance. On the chair summary, I note that he and I both treat B049 and B009 as the first alternatives to each other, which suggests the committee is not far apart on the quality of either. His point that the mechanism does not need to be settled is persuasive, and I would accept it for a prize on the flat-band prediction and the observed states. I still think that eight years is early for the committee to describe how correlated phases are organised, and that is why I would hold B009 until the sample and twist-angle variation Olsson mentions is better understood. I would ask whether he would accept a citation that explicitly avoids the superconducting mechanism and the phase diagram, since that is the form in which I could support it.

uncertainties: Whether Lemonde, Ludlow or another early lattice-clock contributor has a claim strong enough to require a third name, and whether leaving them out can be justified openly in the citation.
How far the 2005 and 2012 prizes should count against a lattice-clock award, and whether a citation centred on the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice is distinct enough in practice.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the formal redefinition of the second, and whether it applies the same maturity standard to B009 and B049.

Whether the published accuracy and stability figures at the 10^-18 level, which no one on the committee has independently verified, hold up under a check of the uncertainty budgets and direct clock comparisons.
Whether the weight I place on B009's open interpretation is itself influenced by working outside condensed matter; I cannot rule that out.
statement.conflict_note: I am updating my round-1 disclosure only slightly. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B049, B009, B026 or B012, which are outside my fields of astroparticle and gamma-ray instrumentation. My profile records work on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite, PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, so I would flag professional proximity and consider recusal if B047 (IceCube neutrinos, Halzen) were seriously considered; it is not in any preferred configuration. As chair, I have noted Kroll's disclosure on B049 and think it should be recorded and not treated as a conflict, but the committee should decide.
